sourceHtml:
Giving supply chain teams direct access to the systems behind their decisions.

Every supply chain generates constant signals: orders in approval, shifting lead times, slowing ports, drifting prices, disruptions. The problem isn’t scarce data. It’s the distance between the data and the decision-maker.

Answering “which top-revenue SKUs are exposed to the current port closure, and what will it cost?” used to mean knowing which system held each piece and stitching them together by hand while the domain expert waited.

Could that manager instead ask in plain language and get an actionable, cross-system answer in seconds? Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is the intelligence layer, exposing enterprise Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers as a composable tool layer. Amazon Quick turns that into action for personas with no setup. Answers come from live systems of record and grounded documents, not model recall, and every change waits for a named human. In this post, we walk through this pattern end to end, from a conversational walkthrough in Amazon Quick to the AgentCore tool layer behind it, and we show you how to deploy it yourself.

The problem: Data-rich, insight-poor

Figure 1: Domain expertise sits with users while operational data is fragmented across ERP, monitoring, procurement, and email

Each question needs its own tool: inventory from the enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, disruptions from email or news, a request for quotation (RFQ) from procurement, and compliance from a checklist. Correlating is manual.

A day in the life

A manager’s morning traditionally spans the ERP (inventory exceptions), monitoring tool (alerts), procurement (alternatives), email (RFQ), and a tracker: 45–60 minutes across five systems with a dozen-plus context switches.

Conversationally it’s three prompts in one tool, “Any critical disruptions affecting my top-revenue SKUs?” → “Assess the TechComp halt and issue an emergency RFQ to approved alternatives” → “Looks good. Send it.”, in minutes.

Figure 2: Traditional multi-tool flow versus a single conversational thread orchestrated by AgentCore

Deep dive: Supply chain scenario walkthrough

The following five steps follow one disruption from detection to an approved emergency RFQ, all in a single Amazon Quick conversation.

Step 1: Discovery – “What tools do I have?”

The user asks “What supply chain tools do I have?” and Amazon Quick lists the supply chain MCP servers published in AWS Agent Registry. Because an administrator has turned on the registry integration, the four business MCP servers already appear as connector cards, with connection details pre-populated and no URLs to enter by hand. The orchestration agent is added as its own MCP connector.

Step 2: Querying – “Show me active disruptions”

“Check active supply disruptions” calls the Disruption Alerts MCP (assess_disruption_impact): three disruptions with severity, region, and SKU counts. How we solve it: Quick routes the request through AgentCore to the MCP server, which queries backend monitoring and returns a structured result, no dashboard or export.

Step 3: Drill-down – “Assess the critical one”

The user opens the TechComp Production Halt. assess_disruption_impact(disruption_id="DISR-002") correlates order, customer, and inventory data: $750K at risk, 23 orders, three days of supply. How we solve it: one MCP tool call fans out across systems of record, so the manager gets a consolidated impact read without touching the ERP.

Step 4: Action – “Get mitigation recommendations”

The user asks for mitigation. recommend_mitigation(disruption_id="DISR-002") chains the Governance MCP (verify approved alternatives) and Quoting MCP (contract-aligned quote), one flow from one request. How we solve it: the agent plans and sequences the calls, so a single ask spans disruption, governance, and quoting with no manual hand-offs.

Step 5: Automated follow-up

The user then sets up proactive monitoring (“Alert me every morning if there’s a new critical disruption”). The same flow can run unattended from an inbound supplier email. How we solve it: the same agent and tools run on a schedule or email trigger, posting review-ready cards to the Activity Feed for a person to approve.

Put end to end, those five steps are a single runtime sequence:

Figure 3: Runtime sequence for the walkthrough, where every result returns to Amazon Quick for approval

Solution architecture

That’s the experience. Here’s how it is built: the pattern separates the intelligence layer from the interface layer, so each evolves independently, with Amazon Quick as the interface and AgentCore as the intelligence.

Figure 4: End-to-end architecture from Amazon Quick to AgentCore (Gateways, Runtime, Identity, Policy) to backends, with AWS Agent Registry alongside

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: The intelligence layer

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a modular agentic platform for building, deploying, and operating agents securely at scale. It offers more than we use here. Four of its services are relevant to this pattern:

  • Runtime – Serverless hosting for MCP servers and agents, with session isolation and built-in identity.
  • Gateway – Turns APIs, AWS Lambda functions, and services into MCP-compatible tools behind a secure managed endpoint, standardizing tool access. Reasoning is the calling agent’s.
  • Identity – Authentication and credential management, compatible with existing identity providers.
  • Policy – Deterministic authorization rules, authored in natural language or Cedar, that intercept every tool call before execution, keeping an agent in its lane on procurement and financial data.

The MCP protocol: How tools communicate

MCP is an open standard for how AI models interact with external tools. Each server exposes tools with typed parameters:

{
  "server_name": "sc-disruption-alert-gateway",
  "tools": [{
    "name": "assess_disruption_impact",
    "parameters": {
      "disruption_id": {"type": "string"},
      "context": {"type": "object"} // order, inventory, revenue data
    }
  }] // plus classify_severity, recommend_mitigation, get_escalation_chain
}

This means:

  • AI clients (Quick, custom agents, other MCP apps) can consume the same servers.
  • Backends (SAP, Oracle, custom microservices) can be wrapped as an MCP server.
  • Tool discovery is automatic. Clients query the registry for schemas at runtime.

AWS Agent Registry: The discovery layer

The registry is the governed discovery layer: a publisher submits a record, a curator approves it, and only then is it discoverable through hybrid search, browsing, or the registry’s MCP endpoint. One scale reality worth noting: because schemas are discovered at runtime, treat each as a contract, versioning new alongside old for breaking changes.

Figure 5: Publishing an MCP server record to AWS Agent Registry, a curator approving it, an administrator linking it to Quick, and approved records becoming connector cards

Multi-step orchestration

The reasoning layer is an agent on AgentCore Runtime, an agent record at its direct invocation URL through a Custom MCP connector, with no Lambda or gateway. Here, it’s the Order Fulfillment Agent. Given one request it plans which tools to call and in what order:

User: "A supplier just went down. Find alternatives, verify compliance, issue an emergency RFQ."
Disruption Alerts MCP -> identify the disruption
Governance MCP -> approved alternatives + compliance + budget authority
Quoting MCP -> contract-aligned quote
-> one consolidated recommendation

Security and governance architecture

Every tool call passes through the same AgentCore control set before it reaches a backend.

Figure 6: The uniform AgentCore control set before the backend (IAM auth, per-tool authorization, input validation, policy evaluation, rate limiting, data-boundary enforcement, audit logging)

The MCP servers in this pattern

MCP server Capabilities Example queries
Quoting Engine (sc-quoting-gateway) Quote generation, pricing rules, validation “Contract-aligned quote for 500 units of SKU-A”
Governance Engine (sc-governance-gateway) Supplier approval, budget authority, regulatory compliance, policy rules “Is SupplierCo on our approved vendor list?”
Invoice Processing (sc-invoice-gateway) Invoice approval routing, AP aging, payment schedules “What invoices are pending approval this week?”
Disruption Alerts (sc-disruption-alert-gateway) Active disruptions, severity, impact assessments, mitigation “Critical disruptions affecting our APAC suppliers?”
Order Fulfillment Agent (sc-order-fulfillment-agent) Multi-step orchestration across all four business MCPs (AgentCore Runtime, direct invocation URL) “A supplier went down, find alternatives, check compliance, issue an RFQ”

Amazon Quick: The enterprise AI assistant

Amazon Quick puts AgentCore tools before business users through chat, agents, the Activity Feed, and automated workflows, with no technical setup.

Key components used

Component Role in this pattern How it works
Agent Registry connection Surfaces MCP servers as connectors Admin links the registry once. Records become connector cards
Quick Agent One SC agent that adapts to role Tailors to persona (manager, procurement, analyst)
MCP connectors Expose MCP tools in chat A card connector exposes tools across Chat, agents, schedules
Activity Feed Proactive alerts and actions Agents post cards. The user acts
Schedules Recurring natural-language automation For example, “every morning”
Outlook Integration Email into the feed Supplier replies parsed and validated
Structured data connectors Query operational records Quick queries Space datasets (orders, inventory, suppliers, contracts) for the MCP rule check
Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) knowledge base Retrieval over documents Invoices, contracts, policies in an S3 knowledge base, grounding answers through Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
CRM connector (optional) Reads customer records (optional) CRM (for example, Salesforce) accounts, opportunities, contacts. Can also load into datasets

Automated Activity Feed and proactive monitoring

The Activity Feed is the proactive surface of Amazon Quick, a unified inbox where agents post results, alerts, and recommendations. Feed items are:

  • Actionable, each carries context and next-step actions.
  • AI-triaged, with priority indicators (Reply needed, Follow up, Deadline).
  • Cross-source, spanning email, schedules, agent runs, and external systems.
  • Human-in-the-loop, where agents propose and humans decide.

How automated monitoring works

AgentCore tools plus the proactive capabilities of Amazon Quick give two paths, time-based and email-driven, through a common trigger → agent → output pipeline.

Figure 7: Three-stage pipeline from trigger (schedule or email) to autonomous agent (assess_disruption_impact, check_supplier_approval, apply_approval_rules, validate_quote) to review-ready card

Use case: Validate supplier responses from email

Suppliers reply to an emergency RFQ by email with pricing. The agent validates each (approved supplier? within guidelines?) and stages the result. It does not author a quote, pick a winner, or issue a purchase order (PO).

Phase 1: Setup (one-time, approximately 5 minutes)

  1. Connect Outlook: in Amazon Quick, choose Settings → Connections → Add Outlook.
  2. Configure Activity Feed: turn on email monitoring in feed preferences.
  3. Create SC Agent: build an agent with these instructions:
Supply chain procurement assistant. On a supplier RFQ reply with pricing: 1) extract SKU(s), quantities, pricing; 2) validate approved vendor (Governance MCP); 3) check pricing within guidelines (Quoting MCP); 4) post a review-ready card (approved-supplier, within-guidelines); do NOT draft a PO or select a supplier.
  1. Create Schedule: “Every 2 hours during business hours, check for new supplier replies and validate them.”

Phase 2: Runtime (fully automated)

Schedule -> email from "TechSupply Co" (MCU-7200, 10,000 units @ $2.45/unit) -> Governance MCP: approved? | Quoting MCP: within guidelines? -> "Supplier Response - Ready for Review" card

The feed card carries the validation results and decision-relevant facts:

Supplier Response: Ready for Review Details
Supplier TechSupply Co, ✅ approved vendor
SKU / Qty / Price MCU-7200 · 10,000 units · $2.45/unit
Price check ✅ within purchasing guidelines
Actions Select for PO · Compare responses · Reject

Phase 3: Human-in-the-loop

The reviewer compares validated responses and either selects a supplier and issues the PO, or rejects with a logged reason. Selection and the PO stay with a person.

Use case: Proactive disruption monitoring

Schedule-triggered, the same pattern applies: a daily 8:30 AM agent checks for new critical or high-severity disruptions, assesses impact, flags anything under seven days of supply as URGENT, and posts an alert card with an Issue Emergency RFQ action.

Where this fits alongside traditional BI

Dimension Traditional business intelligence (BI) / dashboards AgentCore + Amazon Quick
Access model Navigate, log in, find the dashboard/report Ask in natural language. The system finds the source
Time to insight Minutes to hours (find → filter → export → correlate) Seconds (ask → answer with cross-system context)
Multi-system correlation Manual: 3-4 tabs, copy-paste Automatic: the agent orchestrates across MCP servers from one query
Action gap Insight in one tool → switch → act in another Insight → action in the same conversation
Setup cost Weeks/months (dashboard design, ETL, permissions, training) Minutes to connect, once your MCP servers exist
Run cost Fixed: pipelines cost the same whether or not anyone asks Usage-based: serverless scales to zero, cost tracks questions (Lambda + agent tokens)
Trust & accuracy As fresh as the last ETL load Computed live from systems of record and grounded docs, every write human-gated

This isn’t a “replace everything” argument. Dashboards remain superior for trend visualization, collaborative analysis, regulatory reporting, and exploratory analysis. Use conversational AI for real-time operational decisions and BI for strategic analysis. They complement, not compete.

Personas and use cases

One Quick Agent serves all three personas: the manager maintains continuity, procurement sources with compliance-awareness, the analyst correlates signals. Persona also bounds reach, through row/column-level security and per-persona MCP-tool scoping, so procurement does not see finance data.

Persona Use case Tools invoked Outcome
SC Manager Morning disruption check Disruption Alerts MCP Disruptions, revenue at risk, days of supply
SC Manager Emergency procurement Governance → Quoting MCP Verified alternatives + RFQ, one flow
Procurement Supplier verification, budget authority Governance MCP Approval, compliance, limits
Procurement RFQ generation and response validation Quoting MCP RFQ issued + responses validated
Ops Analyst Cross-system correlation SC Operations Agent Multi-MCP reasoning, one query
Ops Analyst Payment queue, audit, disruption trends Invoice / Governance MCP AP aging, audit log, patterns

Getting started

Deploying the pattern takes three phases: provision the infrastructure, connect Amazon Quick to your data and the registry, and turn on monitoring.

Prerequisites

Before you begin:

  • An AWS account with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and AWS Agent Registry.
  • AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) v2, AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) CLI, and Docker (the agent runs as an arm64 container).
  • Python 3.12 or later, with Boto3 1.43.94 or later for the registry step.
  • Active credentials with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions to deploy and register (aws sts get-caller-identity returns the target account).
  • Data layer: a database (Snowflake, PostgreSQL/RDS, or a SQLAlchemy engine), an Amazon S3 bucket, optionally a Salesforce org.
  • Amazon Quick set up for your organization.
  • (Optional) An Outlook account for email automation.

Setup uses two surfaces, so each of the following steps names where it happens: the Amazon Quick web console in a browser (Amazon Quick Sight permissions, Agent Registry linking, connectors, and agent settings) and the Quick Desktop App (connecting Outlook for email automation). The conversational experience in the Desktop App comes last, once setup is done.

Deploy the infrastructure

Everything is open source and scripted: clone the quick-for-supply-chain example in the aws-samples/sample-amazon-quick-suite-knowledge-hub repository and follow its README.md, or point a coding agent like Kiro at it.

The README.md covers three phases. Phase 1 deploys the AgentCore stack: the identity layer (an Amazon Cognito user pool and app client, authorization-code OAuth flow, plus a test user), four business-rule MCP servers (each an AWS Lambda function fronted by its own AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using CUSTOM_JWT authorization), the gateway targets mapping the tools of each Lambda function, and sc-order-fulfillment-agent on AgentCore Runtime as a container, with least-privilege IAM roles. Phase 2 uploads the synthetic dataset to Amazon S3. Phase 3 verifies gateways and runtime are Ready. Six Agent Registry records are approved.

Figure 8: AWS Agent Registry console with six approved records (four MCP Server, one Agent, one Skills)

Grant Amazon Quick access to your data

In the Amazon Quick web console (browser): grant Amazon Quick access from the Amazon Quick Sight admin page (Manage Quick Sight → Security and permissions) to both the S3 bucket and Amazon Athena, since each table is served through an Athena source over an AWS Glue database. Without the Athena grant, dataset creation fails.

Figure 9: Amazon Quick Sight Security and permissions, with Amazon Athena alongside Amazon S3

Link the registry and create connectors

Linking the registry is one-time and administrator-level. Creating a connector is per-user. Both happen in the Amazon Quick console. See the AWS Agent Registry integration guide.

Link the registry (administrator, one-time)

An administrator links one Agent Registry to the Quick account. In the Amazon Quick web console (admin): go to Manage account → Permissions → AWS Agent Registry and turn on the registry (sc-supply-chain-registry, one per account). Only registries in your account and Region, agent-registry namespace, AWS_IAM (SigV4) authorization, and READY status appear. The Quick-managed service role links it.

Figure 10: Linking the registry, where only READY, AWS_IAM registries are selectable

Create a connector

After the registry is linked, approved MCP server records become connector cards: the four business MCPs as cards, the order-fulfillment agent added manually. At scale, federate connector authentication through your identity provider and provision connectors to groups, with the Cognito user pool as the seam.

In the Amazon Quick web console (per user): the four cards appear on the Connectors page (sc-quoting-mcp, sc-governance-mcp, sc-invoice-processing-mcp, sc-disruption-alert-mcp). Authenticate through the OAuth authorization-code flow (OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE) with client ID, secret, and token, authorization, and redirect URLs from the deploy script. Sign in as the test user, turn on tools, create and share.

Figure 11: The four business-MCP connector cards, with the order-fulfillment agent added manually

Registry-sourced connectors are Custom MCP connectors (relevant for custom permissions). Removing the link later doesn’t delete connectors already created.

Figure 12: The Authenticate step using the authorization-code OAuth flow (OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE)

Add the order-fulfillment agent connector

In the Amazon Quick web console: because it is an agent record, create its connector manually (Connectors → Create for your team → Model Context Protocol → Create new): name it sc-order-fulfillment-agent, point it at the AgentCore Runtime direct invocation URL from the deploy script, complete the same OAuth sign-in, create and share.

Figure 13: Creating the sc-order-fulfillment-agent connector, pointed at the AgentCore runtime invocation URL

Attach the connectors to your agent

The deployment creates the Supply Chain agent: a Quick Space, imported datasets and S3 knowledge base, and the agent with instructions, starter prompts, and welcome message. What remains is attaching the connectors.

In the Amazon Quick web console (agent settings): open the deployment-created Supply Chain agent (default id sc-supply-chain-agent) and attach all five connectors (four business MCPs plus sc-order-fulfillment-agent), or pass the five connector IDs to the setup script.

Set up proactive monitoring

To make it proactive, Quick runs the same agent on a schedule or on incoming email and posts results to the Activity Feed. Both paths reuse the agent and tools you configured.

In the Quick Desktop App (Settings → Connections): connect Outlook and turn on email monitoring. Then, in Quick Chat, create two natural-language schedules, time-based (“Every morning, check for new critical disruptions”) and email-driven (“Every two hours in business hours, check supplier replies and validate”). The agent extracts pricing, runs the checks, and posts a card.

Try it in Amazon Quick

With the agent and connectors ready, ask in natural language in Amazon Quick Chat. Each prompt shows the data-then-rules pattern.

Ask Amazon Quick What you get
“What supply chain tools do I have?” The five MCP connectors (quoting, governance, invoice, disruption alerts, order-fulfillment agent), with status.
“Show me active supply disruptions.” Active disruptions with severity, region, SKU counts (Disruption Alerts MCP).
“Assess the impact of the TechComp production halt.” Revenue at risk, affected orders, days of supply, from your datasets.
“Is this supplier an approved vendor, and do we have budget authority for a $72,000 PO?” An approval from the Governance MCP (vendor status, budget authority, compliance).
“Generate a contract-aligned quote for 1,000 units for this customer.” A contract-aligned quote from the Quoting MCP, as a branded document.
“A supplier just went down. Find alternatives, verify compliance, and issue an emergency RFQ.” The Order Fulfillment Agent chains disruption, governance, and quoting MCPs into one recommendation.

Conclusion

AgentCore and Amazon Quick are a repeatable enterprise-AI pattern: separate intelligence from interface. AgentCore turns fragmented backends into a composable, governed, AI-accessible layer through standard MCP interfaces. Amazon Quick democratizes access in natural language.

The gain is the collapsed decision chain: detect, research, decide, act, and log once spanned five tools, now one conversation. The AI researches, correlates, validates. The person decides. Every call is authenticated, authorized, policy-checked, and audited, and a 45-60 minute routine across five systems can collapse to minutes.

That is the shift from data-rich, insight-poor to data-rich, decision-ready. Start with one MCP server and one persona. The registry grows and the experience stays the same.

About the authors

translation.html:
让供应链团队能够直接访问支撑其决策的系统。

每条供应链都在持续产生信号：等待审批的订单、变化的交货周期、运转放缓的港口、波动的价格以及中断事件。问题不在于数据匮乏，而在于数据与决策者之间的距离。

要回答“哪些高营收 SKU 受到当前港口关闭的影响，会造成多少损失？”，过去需要先知道每项信息存在哪个系统中，再手动将它们拼接起来，而领域专家只能等待。

这位经理能否直接用日常语言提问，并在几秒内获得可付诸行动的跨系统答案？Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 充当智能层，将企业的模型上下文协议（MCP）服务器呈现为可组合的工具层。Amazon Quick 则让不同角色的用户无需配置即可将其转化为行动。答案来自实时的权威记录系统和有据可依的文档，而非模型记忆，每项变更都等待指定人员确认。本文将完整介绍这一模式，从 Amazon Quick 中的对话演示，到背后的 AgentCore 工具层，并展示如何自行部署。

问题：数据丰富，洞察不足

图 1：领域专业知识掌握在用户手中，而运营数据分散在 ERP、监控、采购和电子邮件系统中

每个问题都需要使用各自的工具：库存来自企业资源规划（ERP）系统，中断信息来自电子邮件或新闻，询价请求（RFQ）来自采购系统，合规信息来自检查清单。关联这些信息需要手动完成。

日常工作的一天

传统上，经理早晨的工作需要在 ERP（库存异常）、监控工具（告警）、采购系统（替代方案）、电子邮件（RFQ）和跟踪工具之间切换：跨越五个系统，耗时 45–60 分钟，上下文切换超过十几次。

通过对话，只需在一个工具中输入三条提示：“有没有影响我高营收 SKU 的严重中断？”→“评估 TechComp 停产事件，并向获批的替代供应商发出紧急 RFQ”→“看起来不错。发送吧。”几分钟即可完成。

图 2：传统的多工具流程与由 AgentCore 编排的单一对话线程对比

深入解析：供应链场景演示

以下五个步骤围绕一次中断事件，从发现问题到获得批准的紧急 RFQ，全部在一次 Amazon Quick 对话中完成。

步骤 1：发现——“我有哪些工具？”

用户询问“我有哪些供应链工具？”，Amazon Quick 随即列出发布在 AWS Agent Registry 中的供应链 MCP 服务器。由于管理员已经启用注册表集成，四个业务 MCP 服务器已显示为连接器卡片，连接详情已预先填好，无需手动输入 URL。编排智能体则作为独立的 MCP 连接器添加。

步骤 2：查询——“显示当前的中断事件”

“检查当前的供应中断”会调用 Disruption Alerts MCP（assess_disruption_impact）：返回三起中断事件及其严重程度、地区和 SKU 数量。我们的解决方式：Quick 通过 AgentCore 将请求路由至 MCP 服务器，由其查询后端监控系统并返回结构化结果，无需打开仪表板或导出数据。

步骤 3：深入分析——“评估那起严重事件”

用户打开 TechComp 停产事件。assess_disruption_impact(disruption_id="DISR-002") 关联订单、客户和库存数据：面临风险的金额为 $750K，涉及 23 个订单，库存可维持三天。我们的解决方式：一次 MCP 工具调用并行访问多个权威记录系统，让经理无需操作 ERP 即可获得汇总的影响分析。

步骤 4：行动——“获取缓解建议”

用户请求缓解建议。recommend_mitigation(disruption_id="DISR-002") 串联 Governance MCP（核实获批的替代供应商）和 Quoting MCP（生成符合合同约定的报价），一次请求完成一条流程。我们的解决方式：智能体规划调用并安排顺序，因此一次提问就能涵盖中断、治理和报价，无需人工交接。

步骤 5：自动跟进

随后，用户设置主动监控（“如果出现新的严重中断，每天早晨提醒我”）。同一流程也可由收到的供应商邮件触发，在无人值守的情况下运行。我们的解决方式：同一个智能体和同一套工具按计划或通过邮件触发运行，将待审核卡片发布到 Activity Feed，供人员批准。

将这五个步骤首尾相接，就形成一个完整的运行时序列：

图 3：演示流程的运行时序列，每项结果都会返回 Amazon Quick 以供批准

解决方案架构

以上是使用体验。其实现方式如下：该模式将智能层与界面层分离，使两者能够独立演进，其中 Amazon Quick 充当界面，AgentCore 提供智能。

图 4：从 Amazon Quick，经 AgentCore（Gateway、Runtime、Identity、Policy）到后端的端到端架构，旁侧为 AWS Agent Registry

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore：智能层

Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 是一个模块化智能体平台，用于安全地大规模构建、部署和运营智能体。它提供的功能比本文使用的更多。其中四项服务与这一模式相关：

  • Runtime——为 MCP 服务器和智能体提供无服务器托管，具备会话隔离和内置身份功能。
  • Gateway——将 API、AWS Lambda 函数和服务转换为安全托管端点后方的 MCP 兼容工具，统一工具访问方式。推理由发起调用的智能体负责。
  • Identity——提供身份验证和凭证管理，兼容现有身份提供商。
  • Policy——使用自然语言或 Cedar 编写确定性的授权规则，在每次工具调用执行前进行拦截，使智能体在处理采购和财务数据时遵守权限边界。

MCP 协议：工具如何通信

MCP 是一项开放标准，规定 AI 模型如何与外部工具交互。每个服务器都提供带有类型化参数的工具：

{
  "server_name": "sc-disruption-alert-gateway",
  "tools": [{
    "name": "assess_disruption_impact",
    "parameters": {
      "disruption_id": {"type": "string"},
      "context": {"type": "object"} // order, inventory, revenue data
    }
  }] // plus classify_severity, recommend_mitigation, get_escalation_chain
}

这意味着：

  • AI 客户端（Quick、自定义智能体、其他 MCP 应用）可以使用同一组服务器。
  • 后端（SAP、Oracle、自定义微服务）可以封装为 MCP 服务器。
  • 工具发现是自动完成的。客户端在运行时查询注册表以获取架构定义。

AWS Agent Registry：发现层

注册表是一个受治理的发现层：发布者提交记录，审核者批准后，该记录才能通过混合搜索、浏览或注册表的 MCP 端点被发现。规模化时有一点值得注意：由于架构定义是在运行时发现的，应将每个架构定义视为契约；出现破坏性变更时，应让新旧版本并存。

图 5：将 MCP 服务器记录发布到 AWS Agent Registry，由审核者批准、管理员将其关联到 Quick，获批记录随后成为连接器卡片

多步骤编排

推理层是在 AgentCore Runtime 上运行的智能体，其智能体记录通过 Custom MCP 连接器使用直接调用 URL，无需 Lambda 或网关。这里使用的是 Order Fulfillment Agent。收到一个请求后，它会规划调用哪些工具及调用顺序：

User: "A supplier just went down. Find alternatives, verify compliance, issue an emergency RFQ."
Disruption Alerts MCP -> identify the disruption
Governance MCP -> approved alternatives + compliance + budget authority
Quoting MCP -> contract-aligned quote
-> one consolidated recommendation

安全与治理架构

每次工具调用在到达后端前，都会经过同一套 AgentCore 控制机制。

图 6：后端前方统一的 AgentCore 控制机制（IAM 身份验证、逐工具授权、输入验证、策略评估、速率限制、数据边界执行、审计日志记录）

此模式中的 MCP 服务器

MCP 服务器 功能 查询示例
Quoting Engine（sc-quoting-gateway） 报价生成、定价规则、验证 “为 500 件 SKU-A 生成符合合同约定的报价”
Governance Engine（sc-governance-gateway） 供应商审批、预算授权、监管合规、策略规则 “SupplierCo 是否在我们的获批供应商名单中？”
Invoice Processing（sc-invoice-gateway） 发票审批路由、应付账款账龄、付款计划 “本周有哪些发票待审批？”
Disruption Alerts（sc-disruption-alert-gateway） 当前中断事件、严重程度、影响评估、缓解措施 “有哪些严重中断影响我们的亚太地区供应商？”
Order Fulfillment Agent（sc-order-fulfillment-agent） 跨全部四个业务 MCP 的多步骤编排（AgentCore Runtime、直接调用 URL） “一家供应商停摆了，寻找替代供应商、检查合规性并发出 RFQ”

Amazon Quick：企业 AI 助手

Amazon Quick 通过聊天、智能体、Activity Feed 和自动化工作流，将 AgentCore 工具呈现给业务用户，无需技术配置。

使用的关键组件

组件 在此模式中的作用 工作方式
Agent Registry 连接 将 MCP 服务器呈现为连接器 管理员一次性关联注册表。记录随即成为连接器卡片
Quick Agent 一个适应不同角色的供应链智能体 针对用户角色（经理、采购人员、分析师）进行调整
MCP 连接器 在聊天中提供 MCP 工具 卡片连接器让聊天、智能体和计划任务都能使用工具
Activity Feed 主动告警与操作 智能体发布卡片。用户采取行动
计划任务 通过自然语言设置的周期性自动化 例如，“每天早晨”
Outlook 集成 将电子邮件接入动态流 解析并验证供应商回复
结构化数据连接器 查询运营记录 Quick 查询 Space 数据集（订单、库存、供应商、合同），以进行 MCP 规则检查
Amazon Simple Storage Service（Amazon S3）知识库 文档检索 将发票、合同、政策存放在 S3 知识库中，通过检索增强生成（RAG）为答案提供依据
CRM 连接器（可选） 读取客户记录（可选） CRM（例如 Salesforce）中的客户、商机、联系人。也可以加载到数据集中

自动化 Activity Feed 与主动监控

Activity Feed 是 Amazon Quick 的主动服务界面，也是一个统一收件箱，智能体在其中发布结果、告警和建议。动态流中的条目具有以下特点：

  • 可操作，每个条目都附带上下文和后续操作。
  • 由 AI 分流，并带有优先级标记（需要回复、跟进、截止日期）。
  • 跨来源，涵盖电子邮件、计划任务、智能体运行结果和外部系统。
  • 人参与决策，由智能体提出建议，人作出决定。

自动监控的工作方式

AgentCore 工具结合 Amazon Quick 的主动功能，提供基于时间和由邮件驱动的两条路径，共用“触发器 → 智能体 → 输出”这一流水线。

图 7：从触发器（计划任务或电子邮件），到自主智能体（assess_disruption_impact、check_supplier_approval、apply_approval_rules、validate_quote），再到待审核卡片的三阶段流水线

用例：验证邮件中的供应商回复

供应商通过电子邮件回复紧急 RFQ 并提供价格。智能体逐一验证（是否为获批供应商？是否符合准则？）并将结果准备好。它不会编写报价、选定中标者或发出采购订单（PO）。

阶段 1：设置（一次性，约 5 分钟）

  1. 连接 Outlook：在 Amazon Quick 中，选择 Settings → Connections → Add Outlook。
  2. 配置 Activity Feed：在动态流偏好设置中启用电子邮件监控。
  3. 创建供应链智能体：使用以下指令构建智能体：
Supply chain procurement assistant. On a supplier RFQ reply with pricing: 1) extract SKU(s), quantities, pricing; 2) validate approved vendor (Governance MCP); 3) check pricing within guidelines (Quoting MCP); 4) post a review-ready card (approved-supplier, within-guidelines); do NOT draft a PO or select a supplier.
  1. 创建计划任务：“在工作时间内，每 2 小时检查一次新的供应商回复并进行验证。”

阶段 2：运行（完全自动化）

Schedule -> email from "TechSupply Co" (MCU-7200, 10,000 units @ $2.45/unit) -> Governance MCP: approved? | Quoting MCP: within guidelines? -> "Supplier Response - Ready for Review" card

动态流卡片包含验证结果和与决策相关的事实：

供应商回复：待审核 详情
供应商 TechSupply Co，✅ 获批供应商
SKU / 数量 / 价格 MCU-7200 · 10,000 件 · $2.45/件
价格检查 ✅ 符合采购准则
操作 选定并生成 PO · 比较回复 · 拒绝

阶段 3：人参与决策

审核者比较已验证的回复，选择供应商并发出 PO，或拒绝并记录原因。供应商选择和 PO 签发仍由人员负责。

用例：主动监控中断事件

同一模式也适用于计划任务触发：智能体每天上午 8:30 检查新出现的严重或高严重程度中断，评估影响，将库存可维持不足七天的情况标记为“紧急”，并发布带有“发出紧急 RFQ”操作的告警卡片。

如何与传统 BI 配合使用

维度 传统商业智能（BI）/ 仪表板 AgentCore + Amazon Quick
访问方式 导航、登录、查找仪表板/报表 用自然语言提问。系统查找来源
获取洞察所需时间 几分钟到几小时（查找 → 筛选 → 导出 → 关联） 几秒钟（提问 → 获得包含跨系统上下文的答案）
多系统关联 手动：3-4 个标签页，复制粘贴 自动：智能体根据一次查询，跨 MCP 服务器进行编排
洞察与行动之间的间隔 在一个工具中获得洞察 → 切换 → 在另一个工具中行动 在同一对话中从洞察走向行动
设置成本 数周/数月（仪表板设计、ETL、权限、培训） MCP 服务器就绪后，几分钟即可连接
运行成本 固定：无论是否有人提问，流水线成本都相同 按使用量计费：无服务器资源可缩减至零，成本随提问量变化（Lambda + 智能体 token）
可信度与准确性 数据新鲜度取决于上一次 ETL 加载 根据权威记录系统和有据可依的文档实时计算，每次写入都需人工把关

这并不是主张“替换一切”。在趋势可视化、协作分析、监管报告和探索性分析方面，仪表板仍然更有优势。用对话式 AI 进行实时运营决策，用 BI 进行战略分析。两者相辅相成，并不竞争。

用户角色与用例

一个 Quick Agent 服务于全部三类角色：经理维持业务连续性，采购人员在采购时兼顾合规，分析师关联各类信号。角色也通过行级/列级安全控制和按角色限定 MCP 工具范围来约束访问权限，因此采购人员看不到财务数据。

角色 用例 调用的工具 结果
供应链经理 早间中断检查 Disruption Alerts MCP 中断事件、面临风险的营收、库存可维持天数
供应链经理 紧急采购 Governance → Quoting MCP 已核实的替代供应商 + RFQ，一条流程完成
采购人员 供应商核实、预算授权 Governance MCP 批准状态、合规性、额度限制
采购人员 RFQ 生成与回复验证 Quoting MCP 发出 RFQ + 验证回复
运营分析师 跨系统关联 SC Operations Agent 一次查询完成跨多个 MCP 的推理
运营分析师 付款队列、审计、中断趋势 Invoice / Governance MCP 应付账款账龄、审计日志、规律

开始使用

部署这一模式分为三个阶段：配置基础设施，将 Amazon Quick 连接到数据和注册表，然后启用监控。

前提条件

开始之前，需要准备：

  • 一个可使用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 和 AWS Agent Registry 的 AWS 账户。
  • AWS Command Line Interface（AWS CLI）v2、AWS Serverless Application Model（AWS SAM）CLI 和 Docker（智能体作为 arm64 容器运行）。
  • Python 3.12 或更高版本；注册表步骤需要 Boto3 1.43.94 或更高版本。
  • 具有部署和注册所需 AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）权限的有效凭证（aws sts get-caller-identity 返回目标账户）。
  • 数据层：数据库（Snowflake、PostgreSQL/RDS 或 SQLAlchemy 引擎）、Amazon S3 存储桶，以及可选的 Salesforce 组织。
  • 已为你的组织配置好 Amazon Quick。
  • （可选）用于电子邮件自动化的 Outlook 账户。

设置涉及两个界面，因此以下每个步骤都会注明操作位置：浏览器中的 Amazon Quick Web 控制台（Amazon Quick Sight 权限、Agent Registry 关联、连接器和智能体设置），以及 Quick 桌面应用（连接 Outlook 以实现电子邮件自动化）。完成设置后，最后再使用桌面应用中的对话体验。

部署基础设施

所有内容均已开源并提供脚本：克隆 aws-samples/sample-amazon-quick-suite-knowledge-hub 仓库中的 quick-for-supply-chain 示例，按照其 README.md 操作，或让 Kiro 等编码智能体处理该示例。

README.md 涵盖三个阶段。阶段 1 部署 AgentCore 技术栈：身份层（Amazon Cognito 用户池和应用客户端、授权码 OAuth 流程以及测试用户）、四个业务规则 MCP 服务器（每个都是一个 AWS Lambda 函数，前方各自配置 AgentCore Gateway——Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项功能——并使用 CUSTOM_JWT 授权）、映射各 Lambda 函数工具的网关目标，以及在 AgentCore Runtime 上以容器形式运行的 sc-order-fulfillment-agent，均使用最小权限 IAM 角色。阶段 2 将合成数据集上传到 Amazon S3。阶段 3 验证网关和运行时均处于 Ready 状态。六条 Agent Registry 记录获批。

图 8：AWS Agent Registry 控制台，显示六条获批记录（四条 MCP Server、一条 Agent、一条 Skills）

授予 Amazon Quick 数据访问权限

在 Amazon Quick Web 控制台（浏览器）中：从 Amazon Quick Sight 管理页面（Manage Quick Sight → Security and permissions）授予 Amazon Quick 对 S3 存储桶和 Amazon Athena 的访问权限，因为每张表都通过基于 AWS Glue 数据库的 Athena 数据源提供服务。未授予 Athena 权限会导致数据集创建失败。

图 9：Amazon Quick Sight 的 Security and permissions 页面，同时显示 Amazon Athena 和 Amazon S3

关联注册表并创建连接器

关联注册表是管理员执行的一次性操作。创建连接器则由各用户分别执行。两者都在 Amazon Quick 控制台中完成。请参阅 AWS Agent Registry 集成指南。

关联注册表（管理员，一次性操作）

管理员将一个 Agent Registry 关联到 Quick 账户。在 Amazon Quick Web 控制台（管理员）中：转到 Manage account → Permissions → AWS Agent Registry，启用注册表（sc-supply-chain-registry，每个账户一个）。只有位于你的账户和区域中、使用 agent-registry 命名空间、采用 AWS_IAM（SigV4）授权且处于 READY 状态的注册表才会显示。Quick 托管的服务角色负责建立关联。

图 10：关联注册表时，只有处于 READY 状态且使用 AWS_IAM 的注册表可供选择

创建连接器

注册表关联后，获批的 MCP 服务器记录会成为连接器卡片：四个业务 MCP 以卡片形式显示，订单履行智能体则手动添加。规模化使用时，通过身份提供商联合管理连接器身份验证，并向用户组配置连接器，以 Cognito 用户池作为衔接点。

在 Amazon Quick Web 控制台（各用户分别操作）中：四张卡片显示在 Connectors 页面上（sc-quoting-mcp、sc-governance-mcp、sc-invoice-processing-mcp、sc-disruption-alert-mcp）。使用部署脚本提供的客户端 ID、密钥，以及令牌、授权和重定向 URL，通过 OAuth 授权码流程（OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE）完成身份验证。以测试用户身份登录，启用工具，创建并共享。

图 11：四张业务 MCP 连接器卡片，订单履行智能体另行手动添加

来自注册表的连接器属于 Custom MCP 连接器（这与自定义权限有关）。日后移除关联，不会删除已创建的连接器。

图 12：使用授权码 OAuth 流程（OAUTH2_AUTHORIZATION_CODE）的 Authenticate 步骤

添加订单履行智能体连接器

在 Amazon Quick Web 控制台中：由于它是智能体记录，需要手动创建其连接器（Connectors → Create for your team → Model Context Protocol → Create new）：将其命名为 sc-order-fulfillment-agent，指向部署脚本提供的 AgentCore Runtime 直接调用 URL，完成相同的 OAuth 登录，然后创建并共享。

图 13：创建 sc-order-fulfillment-agent 连接器，并指向 AgentCore 运行时调用 URL

将连接器附加到智能体

部署会创建 Supply Chain 智能体：包括一个 Quick Space、导入的数据集和 S3 知识库，以及配置了指令、起始提示和欢迎消息的智能体。剩下的工作是附加连接器。

在 Amazon Quick Web 控制台（智能体设置）中：打开部署创建的 Supply Chain 智能体（默认 ID 为 sc-supply-chain-agent），附加全部五个连接器（四个业务 MCP 加上 sc-order-fulfillment-agent），或将五个连接器 ID 传递给设置脚本。

设置主动监控

为实现主动监控，Quick 按计划或在收到电子邮件时运行同一个智能体，并将结果发布到 Activity Feed。两条路径都会复用你已配置的智能体和工具。

在 Quick 桌面应用（Settings → Connections）中：连接 Outlook 并启用电子邮件监控。然后，在 Quick Chat 中用自然语言创建两个计划任务，分别基于时间（“每天早晨，检查新出现的严重中断”）和由邮件驱动（“在工作时间内，每两小时检查供应商回复并进行验证”）。智能体提取价格、执行检查并发布卡片。

在 Amazon Quick 中试用

智能体和连接器就绪后，在 Amazon Quick Chat 中用自然语言提问。每条提示都展示了先查数据、再执行规则的模式。

向 Amazon Quick 提问 获得的结果
“我有哪些供应链工具？” 五个 MCP 连接器（报价、治理、发票、中断告警、订单履行智能体）及其状态。
“显示当前的供应中断。” 当前中断事件及其严重程度、地区和 SKU 数量（Disruption Alerts MCP）。
“评估 TechComp 停产的影响。” 来自数据集的面临风险的营收、受影响订单和库存可维持天数。
“这家供应商是否为获批供应商，我们是否拥有一笔 $72,000 采购订单的预算授权？” 来自 Governance MCP 的批准结果（供应商状态、预算授权、合规性）。
“为这位客户生成 1,000 件产品的合同合规报价。” Quoting MCP 以带有品牌标识的文档形式生成符合合同约定的报价。
“一家供应商刚刚停摆。寻找替代供应商，核实合规性，并发出紧急 RFQ。” Order Fulfillment Agent 将中断、治理和报价 MCP 串联起来，形成一项建议。

结语

AgentCore 与 Amazon Quick 构成了一种可复用的企业 AI 模式：将智能与界面分离。AgentCore 通过标准 MCP 接口，将分散的后端转化为可组合、受治理且可供 AI 访问的层。Amazon Quick 则让用户普遍能够通过自然语言进行访问。

收益在于决策链条的缩短：发现、研究、决策、行动和记录，过去需要跨越五个工具，如今在一次对话中即可完成。AI 负责研究、关联和验证。人负责决策。每次调用都经过身份验证、授权、策略检查和审计，跨五个系统、耗时 45-60 分钟的例行工作可以缩短到几分钟。

这就是从数据丰富、洞察不足，转向数据丰富、随时可作决策。从一个 MCP 服务器和一种用户角色开始。注册表不断扩展，使用体验保持一致。
